phrases: Yes. Register alpha in context A, and beta in B. Each independent context has its own registry.
Context A finds alpha, but beta is missing. Sharing one Java application doesn't connect these registries.
Create a fresh parent and child. Set the parent before refreshing the child. The registries stay separate.
The child checks locally first. A missing named bean can be found in its parent.
The parent cannot search its children. Our tests confirm both directions: child to parent works; parent to child doesn't.
hook_original: Can two Spring contexts see different beans?
hook_refinement_reason: A shorter spoken question lets the full hook land in about two seconds while the first frame shows different lookup results in separate registries.
semantic_scope: Demonstrated named getBean lookups; fresh parent-child contexts with link set before child refresh; parent instances are not copied to the child.
pronunciation_edit: Add Context before scene3 letter A, so G2P reads the context label as /eɪ/ rather than the indefinite article /ɐ/. No change to inference speed.
